meta: No coding needed: you can build a small AI assistant for your own work. A 5-box plan: who uses it · what one job · what private data · what AI must not do · how to measure it. Then build it in 30 minutes.

muc.title: Now build one yourself
muc.text: In the last six parts, we looked at AI products from the inside. Now let's build one ourselves, no coding needed.

muc.title: A sheet with five boxes
muc.text: Start with a sheet of paper split into five boxes. Box one: who uses it? Box two: what one job does it help them with?

muc.title: The other three boxes
muc.text: Box three: what private data does AI need to know? Box four: what must AI not do? Box five: how will you measure whether it's good?

muc.title: A bakery's plan
muc.text: Take a bakery: regular customers use it. It answers questions about cakes and opening hours. The data is the menu with prices. It never offers discounts on its own. And ten sample questions it must get right.

muc.title: Build it, no code needed
muc.text: Then build it right inside an AI app you know: a custom GPT in ChatGPT, a Gem in Gemini, or a Project in Claude. Use boxes two and four as the instructions, then upload the documents from box three.

muc.title: Try it with real people
muc.text: Run the ten sample questions from box five. Then let three real people try it, and see what they ask that you never thought of.

muc.title: The whole series on one page
muc.text: Engine, fuel, steering wheel, brakes, dashboard. Pick the right task, design for mistakes, measure, count the cost, learn from stumbles. That's the whole series, on one sheet of paper.

muc.title: Fill in five boxes, build in 30 minutes
muc.text: Pick a question customers or coworkers ask you every week. Fill in the five boxes, then build a test version in thirty minutes. Thanks for following the whole series.
